diagnostic_evidence.quote: Therefore any $A\in D\cR (u)$ satisfies $\|A^{-1}\|_\infty \leq \frac{1}{\mu}$.

issues.failure_explanation: A lower bound on eigenvalue moduli does not bound the norm of the inverse of a non-normal matrix. The norm in the lemma is unspecified, and in the Euclidean norm the claim is false. For example, A=[[mu+a,-a],[0,mu]] is row mu-dominant, yet the second column of A^{-1} is (a/(mu(mu+a)), 1/mu), so ||A^{-1}||_2 > 1/mu. The inverse bound does hold in the infinity norm, but only through a different (Varah-type) argument that the proof does not give.

failure_location.quote: By Gershgorin theorem, if $A$ is $\mu$-diagonally dominant, all the eigenvalues of $A$ have complex modulus bigger or equal than $\mu$, and therefore, $A$ is invertible with $\| A^{-1}\| \leq \frac{1}{\mu}$.

issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: State the bound in the infinity norm. Prove it directly: if Ax=y and |x_i| is maximal, then |y_i| >= |A_ii||x_i| - sum_{k!=i}|A_ik||x_k| >= mu|x_i|.
issues.overall_effect: As written, the uniform inverse bound used for Hadamard/Pourciau in the well-posedness theorem is not justified, and the bound is false in the 2-norm.
issues.title: Gershgorin eigenvalue bound does not imply the stated inverse-norm bound
issues.why_classification: A standard few-line argument restores the infinity-norm bound, which is all the theorem needs; no conclusion changes.

Taking the maximum over randomly sampled points yields a value no larger than that supremum, i.e. an underestimate. Such a quantity cannot certify an upper bound on ||u-v||_inf, so the claimed computable a posteriori bound is not delivered.

diagnostic_evidence.quote: For the standard Eikonal equation $|\nabla u| = f(x)$, a common upwind discretization on graphs relies on the neighbor with the minimal value relative to distance:
This is scheme is first derived by Rouy and Tourin \cite{rouy1992viscosity} for Cartesian grids.

issues.failure_explanation: On a Cartesian grid with 2d axis neighbors, max_j (u_i-u_j)_+/dx tends to max_k |d_k u| = ||grad u||_inf, not the Euclidean |grad u|. The displayed scheme is therefore inconsistent with |grad u| = f. It is also not the Rouy-Tourin scheme, which takes the square root of a sum of squared one-sided differences.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Replace it with the Rouy-Tourin form sqrt(sum_k max(D_k^-u, -D_k^+u, 0)^2) = f, or restrict the max-form to graphs with asymptotically dense directions.
issues.overall_effect: The presented upwind example would converge to the solution of a different (l-infinity) eikonal equation.
issues.title: Max-over-neighbors upwind scheme is not consistent with the Euclidean eikonal equation on Cartesian grids
issues.why_classification: This is an illustrative example not used by any theorem; correcting the formula is local.

issues.failure_explanation: With v=(1-e^{-lambda u})/lambda we have v_t = e^{-lambda u}u_t and grad v = e^{-lambda u}grad u. Hence v_t + ||grad v|| = e^{-lambda u}(u_t + ||grad u||) = 0, and no lambda v term appears. Concretely, u=x-t gives v_t+|v_x|=0, so v_t+lambda v+|v_x| = lambda v != 0.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Replace the claim by v_t + ||grad v|| = 0 and remove the assertion that the transform introduces a lambda v term in the evolutive case.
issues.overall_effect: The claimed damping (strict u-monotonicity) obtained by transforming time-dependent problems does not exist.
issues.title: False Kruzhkov-transform equivalence for the time-dependent eikonal equation
issues.why_classification: It is an isolated remark; no theorem or experiment depends on it, so a local correction suffices.

diagnostic_evidence.quote: \dt \ \frac{\partial \cF}{\partial u} (x_j, u, p) \geq - \lambda,
Note that these assumptions allow for numerical Hamiltonians $\cF$ which are not necessarily monotone in $u$, provided the time-step $\Delta t$ is sufficiently small.
By using similar arguments as for the stability of the steady state case.

issues.failure_explanation: The steady-state comparison argument needs the u-monotonicity of (H3). Under (F3), F may decrease in u. Counterexample: F=-c u with 0<c dt<=lambda<1, boundary data equal, and R=0. The scheme gives u^n-v^n = (u^{n-1}-v^{n-1})/(1-c dt), which strictly exceeds the claimed bound. The correct comparison yields only (1-dt||(F_u)_-||_inf)^{-1}(||u^n-v^n|| + dt||R||).
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Either restrict the theorem to F non-decreasing in u, or insert the amplification factor (1-dt||(F_u)_-||_inf)^{-1}. In the latter case, prove it via the max-point comparison and obtain an exp(L_F T)-type Gronwall constant in the recursion.
issues.overall_effect: The non-expansive one-step estimate, and the recursive accumulated error bound derived from it, are invalid in the non-monotone-in-u regime that (F3) advertises.
issues.title: Time-dependent stability estimate with constant 1 is false when F is decreasing in u (allowed by F3)
issues.why_classification: The repair either weakens the estimate to an exponentially growing constant or narrows the hypotheses. The result stays comparable but the stated guarantee changes.

issues.failure_explanation: The Lemma bounds only the diagonal-dominance margin of DR, which scales like h^{d/q}. It gives neither the quadratic-growth constant mu_h of the nonconvex L nor any upper bound on the gradient-Lipschitz constant C_h. In the paper's 1D q=2 setting, C_h ~ ||DR||^2 ~ h^{-1} and mu_h ~ mu^2 ~ h, giving kappa ~ h^{-2}, not h^{-1}. Moreover, a worsening upper bound on ||DR^{-1}|| does not show that the condition number increases.

diagnostic_evidence.quote: L(u,h)- L(u_h^\star,h) \;&\ge\; \frac{\mu_h}{2}\|u-u_h^\star\|_h ^2
Thus, gadient descent with the step size $\eta=1/C_h$ leads to

issues.failure_explanation: For a nonconvex L, quadratic growth together with Lipschitz gradient does not yield linear convergence of gradient descent; a PL-type inequality is needed. Even under PL or strong convexity, step 1/C_h gives E_k <= (1-1/kappa)^k E_0, not exponent 2k. The iteration count k ~ (kappa/2)log(E_0/tol) is therefore off.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Assume a PL inequality with constant mu_h and use E_k <= (1-mu_h/C_h)^k E_0, then propagate the factor-2 change through the iteration counts.
issues.overall_effect: The iteration-complexity formulas underlying the warm-start comparison are not established.
issues.title: Linear GD rate with exponent 2k not implied by smoothness plus quadratic growth for nonconvex L
issues.why_classification: Replacing the assumption and the exponent with the standard PL result is a routine local fix within a heuristic section.

If the coarse problem is solved to a comparable loss tolerance so that the

issues.failure_explanation: Delta k_net = (kappa_h/2)log(E_rand/E_warm) - (kappa_h/4)log(E_rand^{(2h)}/tol) is a difference of positive terms. It is positive only if E_warm < E_rand (tol/E_rand^{(2h)})^{1/2}, which is never verified, and tilde C_h h^{2p} contains C_h, which grows as h->0. diagnostic_evidence.quote: where $a_0 = \left( 1,1, \ldots ,1\right)\in \R^6$
illustrating that the zero-level set successfully wraps around the obstacle constraints while maintaining the correct unit-speed propagation dynamics.

issues.failure_explanation: {g<=0} = B(-a_0,1) ∩ B(0,1/2), and these balls are disjoint because ||a_0|| = sqrt(6) (or sqrt(5)) > 3/2. So g>0 everywhere. Moreover, min(u_t+..., u-Psi)=0 forces u >= Psi, which confines {u<=0} to B(0,1/2). The specified solution is therefore positive for all t, with an empty zero-level set, and the front can never 'wrap around' the obstacle. Psi as written defines an allowed region, not an obstacle.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Correct the formulation, e.g. Psi(x) = 1/2 - ||x|| so the ball is excluded, and confirm that the reported results correspond to the corrected problem, rerunning if necessary.
issues.overall_effect: The high-dimensional obstacle experiment does not support the claimed capability for the problem as specified.
issues.title: Specified obstacle problem has empty zero sublevel set; claimed level-set behavior cannot occur
issues.why_classification: Several sign repairs are possible, and the experimental evidence for an advertised capability must be re-validated against a corrected problem.

diagnostic_evidence.quote: We see that the flow converges to two types of stationary points: ones which correspond to the critical point of $L$, and the others  at which the $\delta L/\delta u$ is orthogonal to the tangent space
this solution is the unique critical point of the functional $L(u)$ defined in \eqref{Lp functional steady state eq}

issues.failure_explanation: The paper proves only that, on a fixed graph, the scheme solution is the unique critical point of L over grid functions. The actual method trains NN parameters by SGD over randomly shifted grids, where parameter-space stationary points need not be critical points of L, as the paper itself notes. No convergence as dx->0 is proved; with fixed damping lambda the scheme even targets a perturbed PDE.

failure_location.quote: By leveraging discrete monotonicity, our approach ensures convergence to the unique viscosity solution, directly addressing the non-uniqueness pitfalls of standard PINNs.

issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Restate the conclusion as uniqueness of critical points of the grid-level residual functional. Present NN convergence and the dx->0 limit as unproven, or as conditional on Barles-Souganidis hypotheses that are verified separately.
issues.overall_effect: The headline guarantee of convergence to the viscosity solution is not established by the paper's results.
issues.title: Conclusion claims guaranteed convergence to the viscosity solution, beyond what is proved
issues.why_classification: The correction withdraws an advertised guarantee, although the proved well-posedness results remain intact.
